I3.findings: 1/ Data inconsistency: the scenario text says the reply went at 09:41, but the sent-mail addition is dated 2026-10-27T10:41+09:00, and the inbound it answers arrived at 09:55. I used 10:41. At 09:41 the mail would predate the action's raised time, so the candidate rule ('since the action was raised') would exclude it and the action would be judged due and RESENT. The outcome depends on that timestamp being right. 2/ Sent scan window (line 40): 'last 24 hours, or back to the start of the latest run whose record isn't Completed if that is earlier'. Read literally, the latest non-Completed record is the 16:38 Skipped one (Skipped isn't Completed), not the crashed 09:38 Started one. The clause therefore adds nothing after a run of skips, and a lock held more than 24 hours would leave the crashed send outside the window. Here the 24-hour window covers 10:41, so the send is found. Suggested wording: 'the earliest run since the last Completed one that took the lock' (or ignore Skipped records). 3/ The crashed send's Cc lacks Jaya and Sarika, which revenue mail requires (line 49). The 17:38 run matches and logs it but has no rule to repair the missing copies, so Jaya isn't on the thread for SLOW 1b's 'she's in Cc' invoice step. 4/ The 09:38 record stays 'Started' forever: no rule makes a later run or the runbook mark it Failed. 5/ Both of Tuesday's SLOW runs (10:38 and 16:38) were skipped, and 17:38 does FAST work only. SLOW work is lost until Wednesday 10:38, with no catch-up rule ('its work stays due' holds only in the sense that it is picked up next time). 6/ The skipped runs follow LOCK step 3 exactly: fetch, M starts 'held:', one record created once, nothing else, no release (line 64: 'never release a lock you don't hold').
